title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's c. 1981 notes 'Autour de la Longue Marche'. S is a connected normal scheme of finite type over Q (characteristic 0 is used explicitly on the previous page). U = X − T is the complement of a divisor T in a relative curve or neighbourhood X/S. E_K, E_S, E_U are the arithmetic fundamental groups (extensions of the absolute Galois group). (13) is an extension of π1(S) by an abelian profinite group, essentially the 'T = T_∞ = Ẑ(1)' of Kummer theory, the inertia at the divisor (cf. (8): I_x ≅ T_∞(K̄*)). This is the 'abelian case' noted in the margin.

Step 1. The multiplicative group G_m(S) = O(S)^* has no nonzero infinitely divisible elements. It is k^* times a finitely generated free group, where k is the number field of constants. The group k^* has no divisible elements, since the units are finitely generated and the valuations are discrete.

Step 2. Hence the Kummer map (27), G_m(S) → G_m(S)^ (profinite completion) → H^1(S, Ẑ(1)), is injective.

Step 3. Conjugacy classes of splittings of (13) form a torsor under H^1(S,T). Grothendieck writes H^1(S,T) ≅ G_m(S)^ in this case.

Step 4. Suppose a certain obstruction vanishes, i.e. (13) admits 'geometric' splittings. It suffices that a section exists (A connected). Then these geometric splittings, coming from actual sections/trivializations, so differing by units, form a torsor under G_m(S) (possibly its completion; see corrections). Via (27) this is a sub-torsor of the H^1(S,T)-torsor of all splittings. This is the Kummer-theoretic picture: geometric sections = discrete G_m(S)-orbit inside the profinite torsor.

Step 5. Grothendieck observes that for the 'perfect description of the absolute algebraic group over Q' (the anabelian dream: recover arithmetic geometry from E_K, π1, etc.) to be complete, one must characterize, purely in terms of that profinite description, this remarkable subset: the image of the discrete units / geometric sections inside their profinite completion. This is a section-conjecture type problem for the non-anabelian G_m case.

Step 6. New paragraph. He wants to understand how a section of extensions of type (1) (generic, over K) can 'specialize' to one of type (2) (sections attached to points: decomposition/inertia groups N_x, I_x of (7)). The next page sets this up via a rational section f of U meeting a section g_i of X at a point s, and the decomposition group of the punctured henselian disc ('rondelle trouée'). This is the specialization of sections toward cusps / tangential base points.
errors: The identification H^1(S,T) ≅ G_m(S)^ is not true in general. Kummer theory gives 0 → G_m(S)^ → H^1(S,Ẑ(1)) → T(Pic S) → 0 (up to lim^1 issues). Equality needs the Tate module of Pic(S) to vanish, e.g. after shrinking S or in the local/henselian situation. Presumably this is implicit in the hypotheses or the 'cas abélien' remark.

The claim that G_m(S) has no infinitely divisible elements is correct for S connected normal of finite type over Q. It fails over e.g. an algebraically closed base field, so the hypothesis 'base Q' (or finitely generated) is essential. The previous page had noted that some statements hold without it.

ideas.what: Kummer map G_m(S) → G_m(S)^ ⊂ H^1(S,Ẑ(1)) is injective because there are no infinitely divisible units over a finitely generated base
ideas.modern_name: injectivity of the Kummer map / Kummer-faithfulness
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Kummer theory); 'Kummer-faithful' terminology due to Mochizuki and Hoshi

ideas.what: Splittings of an extension by Ẑ(1) form an H^1(S,Ẑ(1))-torsor; the geometric splittings form a sub-torsor under units
ideas.modern_name: torsor of sections; cuspidal/tangential sections and their Kummer classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard non-abelian cohomology; the section-conjecture literature (Nakamura, Esnault–Wittenberg, Stix)
ideas.where_published: related discussion in the 1983 letter to Faltings / Esquisse (section conjecture) but not this G_m version

ideas.what: Problem: characterize intrinsically, within the profinite (anabelian) data, the discrete subset of geometric splittings / the image of G_m(S) in its completion
ideas.modern_name: group-theoretic reconstruction of the multiplicative group from Galois data (Kummer theory in absolute anabelian geometry)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Uchida, Neukirch (field reconstruction); Mochizuki (Topics in absolute anabelian geometry, IUT Kummer theory); Hoshi

ideas.what: Specialization of generic sections (type 1) to point/decomposition-group sections (type 2) via the punctured henselian disc
ideas.modern_name: specialization of sections; cuspidal sections and tangential base points ('packets')

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly formulates, as a missing piece of the 'perfect description' of Gal(Q̄/Q)-arithmetic geometry, the problem of characterizing the geometric (Kummer-image of units) splittings inside the profinite torsor of all splittings. This is a G_m/cuspidal analogue of the section conjecture. It anticipates the later program of recovering K^× / O(S)^× group-theoretically (Mochizuki's Kummer theory), but is not documented as Grothendieck's own question.
missed.quote: Pour que la "description parfaite du groupe alg. absolu sur Q" soit complète, il y faudrait également caractériser ... ce sous-ensemble remarquable.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This shows that Grothendieck saw the non-anabelian (G_m, cuspidal) part of the section problem as essential to the Longue Marche program. Historically it links his program to Mochizuki-style reconstruction of multiplicative monoids from Galois groups.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is routine Kummer theory. The page is mildly notable because it records Grothendieck explicitly posing the characterization of the discrete Kummer image inside its profinite completion as part of the anabelian program, a theme later developed by others.
transcription_corrections: 'quand Spl = 0' is uncertain in the image; the symbol is probably a named obstruction or class (e.g. a subscripted letter), not 'Spl'.

'forment un torseur sous [-…-] G_m(S)^' is ambiguous: the crossed-out word is followed by 'G_m(S)' with a superscript that may be a star or hat. Mathematically, a torsor under the discrete G_m(S), sitting inside the G_m(S)^-torsor, fits 'sous-torseur'.
'une section d'extensions des corps du type (1)' is likely 'des groupes' (extensions of fundamental groups), with 'se spécialiser en une [section du] type (2)'.
The last line is likely 'je reprends les notations' (resuming the notations of (7) and (13)) rather than 'comme notations'.
